children: German industry gathered paced in August, shrugging off concerns of a slowdown due to extreme heat, Carsten Brzeski at ING says in a note. "After a setback in July, Germany's cyclical rebound gained new momentum in August...this data suggests that the economic impact of the heatwave and drought in August was less severe than feared," he says. Still, the war in Iran and higher interest rates pose clear risks, Brzeski says. "The renewed increase in inventories could suggest stockpiling by companies, anticipating more supply chain disruptions, and not so much preparing for more production." While the Germany economy appears to be carrying momentum into the third quarter, a sustainable recovery requires more government reforms to improve competitiveness, Brzeski says.
